ideas.children_en: Abraham took another wife named Keturah, who had six sons. Some were tribes in south Arabia. These sons were Abraham's children and they grew up together.

ideas.children_he: הַחְלָטוֹת עַל יְרֻשָּׁה מַשְׁפִּיעוֹת עַל יְלָדִים רַבִּים.
ideas.children_en: Abraham gave all his property to Isaac. The children of the concubines got gifts but no inheritance. Abraham sent them east so they wouldn't compete with Isaac.

ideas.children_he: יִצְחָק וְיִשְׁמָעֵאל נִפְגְּשׁוּ כְּדֵי לִקְבֹּר אֶת אֲבִיהֶם.
ideas.children_en: Abraham lived a long life and died peacefully. He was buried in the Cave of Machpelah with Sarah. Isaac and Ishmael buried him there.

ideas.children_he: גַּם אַחֲרֵי מוֹת אָדָם אָהוּב הַחַיִּים מַמְשִׁיכִים.
ideas.children_en: After Abraham died, God blessed Isaac. Isaac lived in the Negev and took care of sheep, later also farming.
Ishmael, Abraham's son by Hagar, had many sons who led tribes and small nations. They lived partly in tents and in guarded places.

ideas.children_he: כָּל דּוֹר מַשְׁאִיר אַחֲרָיו דּוֹרוֹת חֲדָשִׁים.
ideas.children_en: Ishmael lived 137 years and died. His sons lived from Mahuila to Shur. Ishmael's tribes ruled over Keturah's descendants too.

ideas.children_he: יִצְחָק וְרִבְקָה חִכּוּ זְמַן רַב לִילָדִים.
ideas.children_en: Isaac was 40 years old when he married Rebecca. He prayed to God because they had no children for years, and Rebecca became pregnant.

ideas.children_he: כְּבָר לִפְנֵי הַלֵּדָה הָיָה בָּרוּר שֶׁהָאַחִים יִהְיוּ שׁוֹנִים.
ideas.children_en: Rebecca felt her babies moving strongly. She asked why and God told her there will be two big nations, and the older will serve the younger.

ideas.children_he: לְרִבְקָה נוֹלָדִים תְּאוֹמִים: עֵשָׂו יוֹצֵא רִאשׁוֹן, וְיַעֲקֹב אוֹחֵז בַּעֲקֵבוֹ. יִצְחָק בֶּן שִׁשִּׁים בְּלֵדָתָם.
ideas.children_en: Rebekah gives birth to twins. Esau comes out first, and Jacob holds his heel. Isaac is sixty when they are born.

ideas.children_he: גַּם אַחִים שֶׁגְּדֵלִים יַחַד יְכוֹלִים לֶאֱהֹב דְּבָרִים שׁוֹנִים.
ideas.children_en: When grown, Esau was adventurous and liked hunting. Jacob was quiet and stayed in tents. Isaac loved Esau and Rebecca loved Jacob.
Jacob cooked stew when Esau came back tired from the field after no hunting. Esau was so tired he could barely eat alone.

ideas.children_he: לִפְעָמִים אֲנָשִׁים מְוַתְּרִים עַל דָּבָר חָשׁוּב בִּשְׁבִיל מַשֶּׁהוּ מִיָּדִי.
ideas.children_en: Jacob asked Esau to sell his birthright for the food he was hungry for then.

ideas.children_he: כְּדַאי לַחְשֹׁב עַל הֶעָתִיד לִפְנֵי שֶׁמַּחְלִיטִים.
ideas.children_en: Esau was very tired and didn't think the birthright mattered. Even if valuable, it was far future; Esau didn't plan ahead.

ideas.children_he: הַבְטָחָה שֶׁנּוֹתְנִים בְּרֶגַע שֶׁל חֻלְשָׁה עֲלוּלָה לְהַשְׁפִּיעַ לְזְמַן רַב.
ideas.children_en: Jacob wanted Esau to swear he truly gave him the birthright, making the agreement serious and not just words.

ideas.children_he: עֵשָׂו בָּחַר בָּאֲרוּחָה וְוִתֵּר עַל הַבְּכוֹרָה.
ideas.children_en: Jacob gave Esau food and drink like a meal to show he was serious. Esau ate and left, thinking the deal was not important.
